title: Sample 14-11: Cartoon

illustrates.quote: Multi-Frame Cartoon. A cartoon may have a series of frames. Enclose each frame number in transcriber’s note indicators using 7-5 margins. a. Using 1-3 margins, begin dialogue with the character’s name followed by two spaces. b. Use initial capitalization when dialogue is printed in all capital letters. c. When the dialogue is continued in another frame, repeat the character’s name, followed by two spaces. d. When a character is not identified, an identifying trait is used as the character name, e.g., Boy 1, Boy 2, Man with Hat, etc. e. Give dialogue from an unknown character an identifier, such as “Narrator” or “Unseen Character.” f. If necessary, a brief description of the action in the frame is enclosed in the transcriber’s note with the frame number.

blocks.text: CTRL+ALT+DEL BY TIM BUCKLEY “TOO HARSH” www.cad-comic.com
Speaker names are added by the transcriber.
Frame 1: young Woman and Ethan talking.

blocks.speaker: Woman
blocks.text: Woman  My parents get into town next week, so I need your help cleaning up around here in the next few days.

blocks.speaker: Woman
blocks.text: Woman  Ethan, come on. They’re your parents.

blocks.speaker: Ethan
blocks.text: Ethan  No! They are sadistic people who took pleasure in **torturing** their child.
Frame 3: Ethan is shown as a child playing a video game, while his mother is pointing a finger at him.

blocks.speaker: Mother
blocks.text: Mother  No more video games until you’re done with your homework.

uncertain: The given braille's own leftover print-page-number fragment ('#,-') on line 1, and the exact wrap point of the title/quote/URL paragraph (lines 2-3), are not reproducible by Emboss's 'note' block (which always encloses its ENTIRE text, F-241) — built here as a separate, unenclosed 'paragraph' continuing after 'Cartoon', which gets the right WORDING but not the same wrap margin as the given braille's own TN-continuation cell-5 runover; EXPECTED MISMATCH on those lines, not a gold-file error.
resolution: A/B disagreed substantially: A's own print.blocks already correctly kept the URL right after the title (matching this reconciliation) and used 4 panels/frames; B moved the URL to the very end and modelled 5 print panels (matching the print original's own real panel count, per B's own note, but NOT this EXCERPT's own transcribed frame count — the given braille only ever reaches 'Frame #c', three frames).
